amendments: 2026-11-07 after oracle v1 (rustc-oracle-v1.json): const-call-adapter.rs v1 was rejected by rustc for the fixture itself ("requires `freeze` lang_item": const checking of the const impl body needs it), which is not an outcome. v2 adds core's `Freeze` auto trait and the `auto_traits` feature, as the PA28 source-transmute fixtures do; the case body and the declared outcome 0 are unchanged. Declared before oracle v2.

from-fn-item.rs.reason: core iter::from_fn shape: impl<T, F> Iterator for FromFn<F> where F: FnMut() -> Option<T>; T is determined only by the sugar output equality, and Self::Item in next selects this impl

map-adapter.rs.reason: core Map shape: B determined by F: FnMut(I::Item) -> B; Self::Item in a method where-clause of a second impl with the same where-clause

inline-bound.rs.reason: core RepeatWith shape: the sugar bound is inline on the parameter list, impl<A, F: FnMut() -> A>

caller-premise.rs.reason: a caller premise F: FnMut() -> Option<u8> selects the impl and normalizes <FromFn<F> as Iterator>::Item to u8

caller-mismatch.rs.reason: opponent: the normalized item is u8, returned as u16 (E0308)

output-not-option.rs.reason: opponent: F::Output is u8, so the impl output equality Option<T> cannot hold and no impl applies (E0271 or E0277)

elided-lifetime.rs.reason: core Scan shape: F: FnMut(&mut St) -> Option<B> has an elided lifetime, so the sugar binder quantifies one region; rustc still determines B

explicit-binding.rs.reason: control: the same equality written as F: FnOnce<(), Output = Option<T>> without sugar

const-call-adapter.rs.reason: core array Drain shape: const impl FnOnce<(usize,)> for &mut Drain<T, F> where F: [const] FnMut(T) -> U; U determined by the const sugar bound

impl-lifetime-output.rs.reason: the zero-region sugar body names the impl lifetime: impl<'a, T: 'a, F> Iterator for Borrowing<'a, F> where F: FnMut() -> Option<&'a T>; a caller premise normalizes Item to &'b u8

impl-lifetime-mismatch.rs.reason: opponent: the same normalized &'b u8 returned as &'static u8 (a region error)
